subject: Pioneer Diagnostics — inference fit, topology constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@pioneer-dx.com>; Tom Allen <tom.allen@pioneer-dx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pioneer Diagnostics — inference fit, topology constraints & next steps

Hi Anna / Tom,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the immediate asks so we can keep momentum: 

High-level pain & goals we heard
- Unpredictable latency spikes for clinical summarization pipeline (currently p95 ~750ms; target p95 <= 200ms for 1–2k token summaries).
- Need steady throughput for daily batch ingest (avg ~250 req/s during daytime, short spikes up to ~600 req/s).
- Security & audit: SOC 2 evidence, retention controls, and key management are gating procurement.
- Model quality: you prefer an open 13B-class model (instruction-tuned) with 4k+ context and deterministic output for templated summaries.

Initial topology constraints you called out
- All PHI must stay in VPC or private deployment (no transitive external storage).
- Canary must run in us-east with ability to fail over to hosted fallback for non-PHI workloads.
- Procurement wants clear cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private.

What we recommend (short list)
- Canary: Dedicated small pool (2x A10G equiv) running quantized 13B with KV cache enabled; load-test to validate p95 <=200ms across 1k tokens.
- Routing: latency-first routing for <200ms requests; cost-first for bulk batch jobs with batching window tuned to SLO.
- Fallback: hosted lightweight 7B variant for burst capacity (non-PHI only).
- Observability: enable token-level cost tracing + trace sampling for first 24 hours of canary.

Attachments included
- mutual_action_plan.xlsx (mutual action plan template with milestones)
- pdx-topology-draft.drawio.png (sketch of suggested topology)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 evidence summary and next steps for audit)

Immediate asks / next steps (can we lock these in by EOD Friday?)
1) Pioneer: confirm which workload contains PHI vs non-PHI (two-line list).
2) Pioneer: share a representative payload sample (anonymized) and 1–2 latency-sensitive prompt templates for perf testing.
3) Redwood: we will produce a sizing note (Dedicated vs Private, cost delta) + a POC runbook and a proposed canary date in the next 48 hours.
4) Schedule: propose a 45-min follow-up tech sync (Karthik + Neha + your infra) next week to agree canary window and success criteria.

If that matches what you heard, I’ll drop the mutual action plan populated with target dates and a sizing sketch.

Thanks,
Rachel

Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

> Hi Anna / Tom,
> 
> Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the immediate asks so we can keep momentum:

> High-level pain & goals we heard
> - Unpredictable latency spikes for clinical summarization pipeline (currently p95 ~750ms; target p95 <= 200ms for 1–2k token summaries).
> - Need steady throughput for daily batch ingest (avg ~250 req/s during daytime, short spikes up to ~600 req/s).
> - Security & audit: SOC 2 evidence, retention controls, and key management are gating procurement.
> - Model quality: you prefer an open 13B-class model (instruction-tuned) with 4k+ context and deterministic output for templated summaries.

Thanks — that summary looks right and appreciated. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- PHI scope: only free-text clinical notes and discharge summaries are PHI; metadata (timestamps, IDs) can be processed via hosted endpoints for analytics.
- Payload: we can provide an anonymized sample (remove patient identifiers) by Friday. Which format do you prefer? JSONL with fields {text, template_id, token_count} is best.
- Timeline: procurement needs an initial cost delta for Dedicated vs Private by next Tuesday to decide security budget.

We are encouraged by your canary proposal. For the canary success criteria please include:
- sustained p95 <=200ms across 30-minute test window for single-record requests at 1k token median;
- no more than 2% request error rate;
- KV cache hit >= 40% for repeated templates.

Tom and I are available for a 45-min call Tuesday 11/24 or Wednesday 11/25 (PST) — we prefer Tuesday morning.

Thanks,
Anna Schmidt
Head of Platform | Pioneer Diagnostics
anna.schmidt@pioneer-dx.com | +1 (617) 555-2299

P.S. On attachments: please make the mutual action plan explicit about SOC 2 artifacts and an approximate date to hand off evidence to procurement.

Anna — great, thanks for the clarifications. Quick confirmations: 
- Format accepted: please send JSONL (text, template_id, token_count) by EOD Friday; we’ll keep it in your VPC candidate during the canary.
- Canary success criteria: we’ll bake your three metrics into the runbook (p95, error rate, KV hit).
- Sizing & cost delta: Karthik will send a Dedicated vs Private delta by Tuesday EOD with a nodal cost estimate.

Next actionable items (I’ll own these and drop updates in the MAP):
- Rachel: populate mutual_action_plan.xlsx with milestones + tentative canary week (targeting 11/30–12/04).
- Karthik: sizing note + approximate monthly cost delta (Dedicated vs Private).
- Pioneer: anonymized JSONL payload sample (by EOD Friday).

Scheduling: I’ll propose Tuesday 11/24 10:00 AM PST for the 45-min tech sync — if that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Talk soon,
Rachel
